name: Question 15
problem: A fair coin is tossed $8$ times. What is the probability of getting at most $3$ heads? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be equal to the number of "heads" obtained when tossing a coin.

Here, we have the following information:

- there are $n=8$ tosses

- the probability of getting a "head" is

$$
p=\frac{1}{2}
$$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X∼B(8,\frac{1}{2}).$ 

The number of successes of a binomial random variable has the probability mass function

$$
P(X=x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x},
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments, and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

Substituting the above information into the formula for probability mass function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=x) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{8}{x}){(\frac{1}{2})}^{x}{(1-\frac{1}{2})}^{8-x} \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{8}{x}){(\frac{1}{2})}^{x}{(\frac{1}{2})}^{8-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find the probability of getting a "success" (i.e., a "head") on at most $3$ tosses. So, we compute

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3) & =P(X=0)+P(X=1)+P(X=2)+P(X=3) \\  & ={(\frac{1}{2})}^{8}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{8}{1}){(\frac{1}{2})}^{1}{(\frac{1}{2})}^{8-1}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{8}{2}){(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}{(\frac{1}{2})}^{8-2}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{8}{3}){(\frac{1}{2})}^{3}{(\frac{1}{2})}^{8-3} \\  & ={(\frac{1}{2})}^{8}+8(\frac{1}{2}){(\frac{1}{2})}^{7}+28{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}{(\frac{1}{2})}^{6}+56{(\frac{1}{2})}^{3}{(\frac{1}{2})}^{5} \\  & =0.363\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Question 15
?

A fair coin is tossed 8 times. What is the probability of getting at most 3 heads? Round your answer to 3 decimal places.

a
0.328
b
0.363
c
0.345
d
0.297
e
0.289
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let the random variable X be equal to the number of "heads" obtained when tossing a coin.

Here, we have the following information:

  • there are n=8 tosses

  • the probability of getting a "head" is p=12

So, X follows a binomial distribution, where X∼B(8,12).

The number of successes of a binomial random variable has the probability mass function

P(X=x)=(nx)px(1−p)n−x,

where n is the number of experiments, and p is the probability of success on each experiment.

Substituting the above information into the formula for probability mass function, we get

P(X=x)=(8x)(12)x(1−12)8−x=(8x)(12)x(12)8−x.

We want to find the probability of getting a "success" (i.e., a "head") on at most 3 tosses. So, we compute

P(X≤3)=P(X=0)+P(X=1)+P(X=2)+P(X=3)=(12)8+(81)(12)1(12)8−1+(82)(12)2(12)8−2+(83)(12)3(12)8−3=(12)8+8(12)(12)7+28(12)2(12)6+56(12)3(12)5=0.363

rounded to 3 decimal places.
